model_note: Owner-FCF DCF on the ENTERPRISE (component build, 10-year, leases as operating cost) with equity as the residual after pro-forma net borrowings, and a distress-weighted scenario set. WasteCo straddles three routing rows in .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md -- 'operating company, non-US/cyclical', 'distressed' and 'live corporate action' -- and this hybrid is the deliberate resolution: it is an operating going concern ($70.2m revenue, +$5.6m operating cash flow, >45% contracted council/commercial revenue, an executed $10m receivables facility, a Kiwibank waiver and facility variation agreed 5-Aug-2026, and a live placement/SPP), so a pure asset/creditor waterfall (the AFC.NZ treatment) would discard real forward cash flows; but it carries an audited material-uncertainty going-concern paragraph, a second covenant breach in two years, all core bank facilities maturing 30-May-2027, and net assets of $3.2m against $58.1m of debt and leases, so a plain three-growth-scenario DCF would ignore that the equity is a deeply subordinated residual. The bear scenario IS the creditor waterfall expressed through the engine: negative owner FCF every year, terminal value on the zero floor, EV below net debt. Raw (negative) per-share values are carried into the weighting per the folder convention (SML.NZ, AGL.NZ, MPG.NZ); floored twins are reported alongside because a limited-liability share cannot be worth less than zero.

inputs.share_count_basis: Pro-forma fully diluted for announced, in-flight issuance only: 1,098,372.765k on issue at 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 annual report note 19; unchanged at 29-May-2026 per the annual report) + 285,714k placement at $0.007 (2-Sep-2026 offer, $2.0m minimum, closes 25-Sep-2026, NOT underwritten) + 107,143k SPP at $0.007 (11-Sep-2026, $0.75m sought, closes 30-Sep-2026) + 12,001k from the mandatory conversion of the $700k 17-Aug-2026 notes at $0.05833 on completion of the raise. Oversubscriptions ($1.0m placement, SPP at discretion) are NOT assumed. Excluded as out of the money: 24.4m options at $0.030 weighted exercise price; $2m unsecured notes convertible at $0.007 (285,714k shares; in the money only in the bull -- see intrinsic_value_if_converted); $15m Empire secured notes convertible at $0.02 (750,000k shares). Count held FLAT across the projection because SBC is expensed in the flows. Replace with the actual allotment on 30-Sep/7-Oct-2026 and with the H1 FY2027 balance sheet when published.

contingent_dilution.note: If every instrument converted the count would be ~2.56bn. The $15m Empire notes (6% cash coupon, secured second-ranking, mature 19-Dec-2029) are held by the family office of the Chair, Sean Joyce.

net_debt_bridge.item: Borrowings at carrying value, 31-Mar-2026 (overdraft 4,122 + asset finance 21,912 + convertible notes 13,046 + other loans 1,016)
Uplift convertible notes from carrying value to face ($15m + $2m)
= audited net borrowings ex-lease, convertibles at face
less cash from $700k convertible notes issued 17-Aug-2026 (note itself converts to shares, so no debt)
less placement proceeds at the $2.0m minimum (2-Sep-2026)
less SPP proceeds at the $0.75m sought (11-Sep-2026)
less non-core asset-sale proceeds applied to debt (management target $10-12m, 2-Sep-2026 fact sheet; haircut to $8m; divested flows excluded from projections per section 7(d))
= net debt used in the equity bridge

inputs.net_debt_note: Lease liabilities ($17,988k at 31-Mar-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt because the full lease cash cost (principal 3,090 + interest 1,334 = 6.3% of revenue) is charged inside the flows -- lease treatment (B), one treatment only. Convertible notes are taken at FACE ($17m) not carrying value ($13,046k): they are repayable at par if unconverted. The balance sheet is six months stale and the direction since March is worse (half a year of ~$3.3m/yr cash interest, a negative FY27 H1 owner-FCF, drawings on the Pacific Invoice Finance facility, and 'active management of trade creditors' per the fact sheet); none of that drift is estimated here. The $8m asset-sale credit is a management target, not a realised amount; every $1m of shortfall is -$0.00067/share.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest received was $9k on $1.2m of cash against $40m of borrowings -- not net cash, so nothing is stripped (owner-fcf.md section 1(b)).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note 20 (share based payments reserve: options issued 76) and note 7.1 (labour expenses: share based payments 52 + directors 24). WARNING for the parser: the Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column (405/564/411/323) is the RESERVE BALANCE, not the annual expense (FY23 405, FY24 275, FY25 -60 net reversal, FY26 76). Immaterial at ~0.1% of revenue either way.
inputs.last_fcf_identity: last_fcf = reported_fcf (OCF 5,557 - capex 1,809) - lease_cash_deducted 4,424 - sbc 76 - interest_income 0 = -752. Intangible capex ($69k) and asset-sale receipts ($1,317k, non-recurring) excluded from reported_fcf.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in any period; the flat count is a modelling convention, not something the company funds.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-18T01:48:47Z (Yahoo regularMarketPrice, Friday 18-Sep-2026 13:48 NZST regular session; 52w range 0.005-0.019). The price equals the live placement/SPP issue price of $0.007 -- it is anchored by the raise until allotment (30-Sep / 7-Oct-2026).
inputs.balance_sheet_source: FY2026 annual report (audited, Deloitte-signed 28-May-2026, released NZX 29-May-2026, announcement 473636); pro-forma items dated 17-Aug-2026 (478008), 2-Sep-2026 (479063/479085), 11-Sep-2026 (479561), 18-Sep-2026 (480144)
inputs.guidance_fy2027: 2-Sep-2026 fact sheet: FY27 Operating EBITDA 'the same or similar to FY2026' ($5.85m reported / $6.73m adjusted); net loss reduced by $2.5-4m; ~$5m annualised cost-out; $10-12m non-core asset sales; FY28 'full year of cost reductions of $5-6m', revenue and EBITDA 'to grow significantly'.
inputs.units_note: All money values NZ$000 (matching the filings and Metrics.csv); share counts in thousands; per-share values in NZD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.4% (Sep-2026) + 5.5% ERP x beta 1.1 + ~3% small/illiquid-cap premium = ~13.5% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~9% (asset finance 7.2% weighted FY26, overdraft 9.6%, convertibles 6-10% cash / 14-18% effective) with NO tax shield while losses persist; normalised 50/50 structure = 11.2%, rounded to 11%. The company's own impairment-test WACC is 9.5% (annual report note 16.1). Going-concern and refinancing risk is charged ONCE, in the 45% bear weight -- not stacked into WACC and not varied by scenario (owner-fcf.md section 7(f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- full lease cash (principal + interest, both from the cash-flow statement) charged in the flows at 6.3% of revenue; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; D&A for tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26: 9,749 - 3,040 = 6,709 = 9.55% of revenue).
notes: MODEL CHOICE: owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10-year, treatment-B leases) on the enterprise with equity as residual, plus a distress bear and a 45/35/20 weighting. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md; see model_note for why neither a pure asset waterfall nor a vanilla DCF fits.
HORIZON: 10 years because the year-5 owner-FCF margin (base 2.5%) is still below its mature level (2.7%); the bull is also still maturing at year 5.

FLOW FORMULA (dashboard component engine): EBIT = revenue x (EBITDA margin - SBC% - lease% - D&A%); cash tax on max(0, EBIT); FCF = EBIT - tax + D&A - capex + wc_capture x (revenue change). Terminal value = max(0, min(Gordon, cap x FCF_10)).

TERMINAL: base cap 12x binds (Gordon at 11%/2.5% is 12.06x); bull Gordon binds inside a 14x cap; bear is on the zero floor. Caps are below the house 20x because this is a fleet-heavy, sub-scale, cyclical-exposed service business.

ASSET SALES: $8m of the $10-12m target credited in the bridge as a non-operating inflow; the divested divisions' flows are removed from the projections (FY27 growth 1.5% net of exits and the Ashburton start). Held constant across scenarios so the dashboard engine reproduces every scenario from one bridge.
SBC-ZERO MARKET: SBC is ~0.1% of revenue; rows kept explicit; house/street band collapsed, band_position null.

WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventory (8.8m) ~ payables (9.4m); wc_capture -5% because growth in council contracts is receivables-led. The FY26 payables stretch ('actively managing trade creditors') will unwind as a one-off outflow that is not modelled.

TAX: NZ 28% statutory; accumulated losses ~$26m and EBIT negative until ~FY32 in the base, so cash tax is zero for six years then ramps 14% -> 28%. NZ shareholder-continuity / business-continuity rules could forfeit losses on a control-changing recapitalisation -- immaterial here because EBIT is ~0 when tax starts.

STALE ANCHORS: price is pinned at the raise price; net debt and shares are 31-Mar-2026 plus announced items. First refresh: allotment notices (30-Sep / 7-Oct-2026), then the H1 FY2027 result (Nov/Dec 2026), then the Kiwibank refinancing outcome before 30-May-2027.

historical_growth.history_basis: FY2023-FY2026 only (three years). WasteCo reverse-listed into Goodwood Capital in December 2022; FY2022 and earlier are the shell / pre-listing entity and are excluded. No five-year CAGR exists.

owner_fcf_history.basis: OCF - PP&E and intangible capex - lease principal - lease interest - SBC expense (treatment B; pre debt interest). NZ$000.

FY2026.note: -752 in inputs.last_fcf excludes the $69k intangible capex

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case organic revenue growth (FY28-FY31 path). The 26.9% revenue CAGR was bought with debt and acquisitions (Cleanways FY24, Civic Waste Nov-24) and is not repeatable; the -31.3% equity CAGR describes value destruction, not a growth anchor.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR -31.3% vs revenue CAGR +26.9%: revenue doubled while equity fell 68% -- growth was funded with debt and produced losses every year. EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are null because both endpoints are negative.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF was negative in three of the four years since listing and the positive FY2025 (+$0.7m) was a capex-starved year (capex $1.0m against $6.2m of ex-ROU depreciation). The business has never covered its fleet-and-lease cost from operations before debt interest of $3.1-3.2m/yr.

base.narrative: Turnaround partly delivers and the lender keeps rolling. FY27 operating EBITDA flat on FY26 (8.3%) per the fact-sheet guidance, then roughly $3m of the targeted $5m annualised cost-out sticks from FY28 (11%), rising to a 14% mature margin by FY32 -- below WasteCo's own FY23 16.2% and well below the landfill-owning majors. Revenue grows 1.5% FY27 (divestments net of the Ashburton start), 3.5% FY28 (full Ashburton year), fading to 2.5%. Fleet renewal keeps costing 6.3% of revenue in leases plus capex ramping 4% -> 4.5%, so owner FCF matures at only ~2.7% of revenue. The placement and SPP complete at the announced minimums, the $700k note converts, $8m of the $10-12m asset-sale target is realised and applied to debt, and Kiwibank refinances in May 2027. Even so, EV of ~$18.5m does not cover $31.4m of pro-forma net borrowings: the equity is a residual claim below zero on a DCF basis.

bull.narrative: Management's plan lands close to its own numbers. Full $5-6m cost reduction from FY28, 5% revenue growth FY28-FY30 (Ashburton, M&Q expansion, national tenders unlocked by Civic), EBITDA margin 13% FY28 rising to 17% by FY31 and held (above the FY23 16.2% peak). Fleet cost unchanged (6.3% leases + 4-4.5% capex), 28% tax once losses are used. Terminal value binds on Gordon at 2.5% (12.1x FCF), inside the 14x cap. EV of ~$39.7m clears pro-forma net borrowings by ~$8m -- about $0.0055/share, i.e. the placement price. The $2m note (conversion price $0.007) would convert at this value; the $15m Empire notes ($0.02) would not. A trade sale at 8x FY28E EBITDA (memo) is the only path materially above the current price.

bear.narrative: Turnaround stalls and the balance sheet resolves against equity. The $5m cost-out slips, the divested divisions take revenue with them (-3% FY27, flat FY28), operating EBITDA margin drifts 7.5-10% and never covers the 6.3% lease charge plus 3.5-4.5% fleet capex, so owner FCF is negative every year and the terminal value sits on the zero floor. In May 2027 the $21.8m of Kiwibank core facilities are not rolled on acceptable terms; the outcome is either enforcement under the first-ranking GSA or a rescue recapitalisation (Empire converting its $15m secured notes / a debt-for-equity swap at or below $0.007) that leaves existing holders with a sliver. The WorkSafe prosecution and the second fatality weigh on council re-tenders. Asset sales realise less than $8m in a forced process (not varied in the bridge; worth ~-$0.003/share on top).

bear.floor_flag: Terminal FCF is negative in every projected year; TV = max(0, min(Gordon, cap)) = 0. A bear case on the floor means the business does not survive that path as a going concern.

entry_price.method: 15% IRR: PV of interim owner FCF at 15% + PV of terminal value REBUILT at 15% (min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF_10)) - net debt bridge, per share; computed for all three scenarios and probability-weighted.
entry_price.note: Every scenario's 15%-hurdle entry price is NEGATIVE: there is no positive price at which the modelled equity flows return 15%, because pro-forma net borrowings exceed the enterprise value at a 15% discount rate in all three cases (bull EV at 15% is ~$25.3m against $31.4m of net debt). The actionable reading is that a 15% equity IRR from here requires an outcome outside the DCF -- a trade sale at an EBITDA multiple (see valuation_memos.trade_sale_reference) or a restructuring in which existing holders are not the residual.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that rate (cap 12x). The 11% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. Negative throughout: at no discount rate down to 9% does base-case EV cover net debt.

sensitivity.matrix_units: NZD per share (rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth)
sensitivity.note: Rows are nearly flat across terminal growth because the 12x FCF cap binds at every WACC <= 11%; only at 12-13% does Gordon fall inside the cap. No cell is positive.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 45%: audited material-uncertainty going-concern paragraph; second Kiwibank covenant breach in two years (Sep-2024, Mar-2026) with a waiver that was only conditional at balance date; ALL core Kiwibank facilities ($6.4m + $15.4m) now mature 30-May-2027 after the 5-Aug-2026 variation; negative working capital $28.7m; FY27 EBITDA guided flat, so interest cover stays ~1.1x; the placement and SPP are not underwritten and both closing dates have already been extended (soft demand at $0.007); management is stretching trade creditors; two workplace fatalities and a live WorkSafe prosecution in front of council customers; interim leadership churn (three board resignations in 2026, new CEO Aug-2026). Base 35%: the bank has waived twice and varied rather than enforced; a $10m receivables facility is executed; the Chair's family office has $15m of secured notes at stake and a stated intent to keep the company alive; operating cash flow is positive and growing; $10-12m of asset sales would halve senior bank debt. Bull 20%: the plan is credible in outline (cost-out, Ashburton, M&Q) but needs several independent things to go right -- cost-out landing in full, revenue growth despite exits, no council tender losses from the H&S record, and a May-2027 refinancing on tolerable terms -- and it only reaches the current price. Even the bull weight is generous to the equity relative to the DCF: it is retained because the market is visibly pricing a trade-sale option that the DCF does not capture.
probability_weighted.floor_note: weighted_iv carries raw (negative) scenario values per the folder convention; weighted_iv_floored applies max(0, IV) per scenario, the limited-liability reading. Both say the same thing: the probability-weighted DCF value of the equity is ~zero and the $7.7m market capitalisation is option value.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street values differ by < $0.0006/share because SBC is ~0.1% of revenue (SBC-zero market); the accounting-regime band has collapsed to a point, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0%.

trade_sale_reference.method: 8.0x FY2028E operating EBITDA (post-IFRS-16, lease-inclusive EV) less lease liabilities scaled with revenue, less the same net-debt bridge; the multiple NZ/AU waste consolidators have paid for contracted collection businesses. Memo only -- NOT the house basis (owner-fcf.md section 7, 'no re-rate reference value' logic in reverse).
trade_sale_reference.reading: A probability-weighted trade sale at 8x FY28E EBITDA is worth ~$0.0070/share -- essentially the $0.007 placement price. That is the case the market (and the Chair's fact sheet, which cites 'unsolicited approaches from significant third-party investor groups') is pricing. It requires a buyer to pay 8x for a 11-13% margin business and the turnaround to be visible by FY28; the house DCF, which capitalises the thin owner-FCF the fleet cost leaves behind, does not get there.

market_implied.note: Lease-consistent: lease-inclusive EV over post-IFRS-16 EBITDA. At $0.007 the market pays ~11.8x reported / ~10.2x adjusted FY26 EBITDA for a loss-making, going-concern-qualified operator -- a full multiple that only makes sense as a bet on the turnaround plus a strategic exit.

liquidation_cross_check.method: Forced-sale realisation of 31-Mar-2026 assets against claims, ranking: Kiwibank first-ranking GSA, Empire second-ranking GSA, unsecured.
liquidation_cross_check.reading: Realisable assets of ~$31m cover Kiwibank and roughly a third of Empire's secured notes; unsecured creditors and shareholders receive nothing. This is what the bear scenario's zero floor means in balance-sheet terms.

valuation_philosophy.what_the_equity_is: A deeply subordinated residual: $58m of debt and leases sits ahead of $3.2m of book equity in a business whose owner FCF, after the 6.3%-of-revenue lease charge and fleet capex, has never covered its ~$3.2m/yr of cash debt interest. On the house DCF the probability-weighted value of that residual is zero or below; the $7.7m market capitalisation is the option value of (a) the turnaround plan delivering management's own FY28 numbers and (b) a strategic buyer paying an EBITDA multiple.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_an_asset_model: Unlike AFC.NZ, WasteCo is a real operating business with $70m of revenue, positive and growing operating cash flow, contracted council work, an executed working-capital facility and a cooperative senior lender. Its forward flows are the right thing to discount; the distress lives in the bear weight and in the fact that EV is compared against a net-debt bridge it does not clear.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: Upward: placement/SPP oversubscribed and allotted; asset sales at or above $10m applied to Kiwibank; H1 FY27 operating EBITDA visibly above $3.4m (i.e. run-rate above FY26) with the cost-out evidenced; a binding strategic investment or takeover approach; Kiwibank refinancing beyond May 2027 announced. Downward: raise closes short of $2m; further covenant waiver requests; WorkSafe conviction with council contract consequences; Empire converting or a debt-for-equity swap below $0.007.
valuation_philosophy.reconciliation_with_price: The market price coincides with the placement price and with a probability-weighted 8x-EBITDA trade-sale memo (~$0.0067). It does not reconcile with the house DCF at any WACC in the 9-13% grid. A buyer at $0.007 is underwriting the trade-sale case, not the cash flows.

data_quality_flags: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp holds the share-based-payment RESERVE balance (405/564/411/323), not the annual expense (405/275/-60/76). Fix via make fix if the column is ever load-bearing; immaterial for this valuation.

Metrics.csv EBITDA is segment-total Operating EBITDA (post-IFRS-16, before H&S reset, restructuring and acquisition costs). FY26 one-offs below that line were $3.1m; the company's 'adjusted' FY26 EBITDA of $6.73m adds back further items inside operating EBITDA and includes $210k of insurance proceeds.
CapEx in Metrics.csv is PP&E only (1,809); intangibles (69) and asset-sale receipts (1,317) are excluded from reported_fcf here.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
